content:
Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
Do not use tools, subprocesses, dynamic code execution, or additional model interfaces.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically unless you reply SELECT followed by a listed successful step
number to retain an earlier build. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.
Never claim that code returned after execution exhaustion has been built or validated.

Shared reconstruction procedure:
1. In short code comments record an inventory of visible objects, partial/cropped objects,
   dominant architectural edges, near/far anchors and occlusion order. Use semantic names.
   Record uncertain dimensions and hidden geometry as hypotheses, not measurements.
   Pick a consistent arbitrary world scale; absolute scale is not identifiable from this image.
2. Parameterize camera position, target, lens and object dimensions separately. Fit room edges,
   vanishing directions and several anchors at different depths before fine object sizing.
   Focal length changes framing throughout the image; local object scaling changes a subset.
   Depth, orientation and occlusion also affect apparent size. A single score delta cannot
   identify the cause, and a failed positive perturbation does not justify its inverse.
3. Build a modest complete scene first. Preserve visible counts, silhouettes, negative spaces,
   supports and cropped foreground objects before adding surface decoration. Prefer procedural
   materials for dense grain/weave and a few SceneAct segments for curves. fillet_box creates
   many meshes; sweep_tube creates a rod per segment and a ball per point. Avoid thousands of
   decorative objects. This is a runtime heuristic, not a measured universal complexity limit.
4. Group every movable semantic object as an Asset containing all its relevant parts: supports,
   rails, trim and fittings as well as its main surfaces. Keep room architecture outside furniture
   groups. Do not create detached bpy geometry as a performance workaround. All geometry must
   remain represented in the SceneAct graph. Retain stable semantic child keys across revisions.
5. Derive support heights and offsets from shared dimensions or named anchors. Use explicit
   anchors for snap/bind. Bind only endpoints already in the scene, never ancestor to descendant;
   avoid cycles and competing bindings. Capture returned copies from layout functions. Use the
   node returned by include when ownership may cause a clone. Recheck support gaps and neighboring
   clearance after resizing. AABB anchors are approximations for curved or rotated geometry;
   overlaps within a fillet assembly do not establish a physical collision.
6. Before adding an apparently missing item, inspect its construction and membership: an item may
   be absent, replaced by a duplicate include key, cropped, hidden behind another item, or too small.
   Preserve legitimate occlusion; do not enlarge or move objects solely to expose every part.
7. For each revision state the observation, hypothesis, affected object/module, dependencies,
   intended change and preservation risks in short comments. Use unknown for unresolved mappings.
   Prefer one revision family per render. Changes required for coherent supports/attachments belong
   to the same family. Keep unrelated camera/geometry/material settings stable. Review the next
   actual render for both the intended effect and collateral changes.

Source preflight before EVERY execution:
- Dimensions/radii must be finite and positive. For fillet_box, 0 < radius <= min(size)/2;
  thickness is included in this bound. Use a box or a smaller valid radius for thin slabs.
- Rod endpoints must differ. Consecutive sweep points must differ; close a loop only once.
- parent.include replaces an existing child under the same key. Repeated elements need unique
  keys, preferably indexed within a semantic Asset. Do not silently overwrite repeated parts.
- Include all composite parts before transforming the parent. Use an explicit pivot when the
  intended pivot differs from its AABB center. SceneAct parent origins may be world zero.
- realize clears Blender. Create camera, lights, world and custom materials AFTER realize.
  Before using the world, write:
      sc = bpy.context.scene
      if sc.world is None:
          sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('Ambient')
      sc.world.use_nodes = True
  Then access its Background shader. Do not assume a startup world survives realization.
- Material customization must use semantic ownership, not scene-wide color matching. The compiler
  may share materials between equal finishes. Copy a material before a local edit when it also has
  users outside the intended subtree. Preserve non-target shader values, geometry and parenting.
- Audit composite movement through descendant membership: all intended parts must move together,
  and unrelated objects must stay outside the group. A prescribed movement/material pass certifies
  the tested operation only, not semantic completeness, true support or metric reconstruction.
- Keep an active camera, finite geometry and independent editable objects. Do not change fixed
  runner settings, evaluation rules, acceptance criteria or resource limits.

Failure handling: a missing output or failed execution is a failure, not a visual observation.
Repair explicit exceptions first, preserving unrelated code. For a timeout, simplify costly
surface repetition and curve sampling without dropping major objects or bypassing SceneAct.
Inspect a successful render before claiming visual improvement. Do not spend an execution on
an unchanged program or a diagnostic-only scene that cannot serve as the final reconstruction.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
It returns the attached node; if node belongs to another parent it attaches an independent clone.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='center', target_anchor=None, offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
For an Asset target, omitted target_anchor uses source_anchor. For support placement explicitly
use source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top'. A point target has no target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='center',target_anchor='center',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
For support bindings explicitly specify source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top'.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)
